hero.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested for swinging bat at children riding bicycles
hero.body:
A Port St. Lucie man was arrested after police say he swung a bat at children who were riding bicycles in the area. The arrest was announced Monday by local authorities.

Police took the man into custody following the incident involving the children. Investigators say the man threatened the young bicyclists with the baseball bat during the confrontation.

The suspect now faces criminal charges related to the attack on the children. Authorities have not released the identities of the children involved or their ages.

The man remains in custody as the investigation continues. Police have not disclosed what prompted the incident or where exactly in Port St. Lucie it occurred.

cards.headline: Boynton Beach man arrested in April fatal shooting of Plantation father in Boca Raton parking lot
cards.teaser: Willie Byrd Jr., 42, was arrested Friday and charged with first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of Arman Motiwalla, who was found with multiple gunshot wounds in a Boca Raton parking lot on April 8.
cards.body:
Willie Byrd Jr., a 42-year-old Boynton Beach man, was arrested Friday and charged with first-degree murder with a firearm in the death of Arman Motiwalla, a 37-year-old Plantation father shot in a Boca Raton parking lot in April. Motiwalla was discovered with multiple gunshot wounds next to his car around 1:45 a.m. on April 8 in the parking lot of 350 Camino Gardens Boulevard. According to a probable cause affidavit, surveillance footage captured the shooting on the evening of April 7, and investigators say Motiwalla's Apple Watch recorded his last heartbeat at 8:25 p.m. Police had offered a $3,000 reward for information leading to an arrest.

The investigation revealed Byrd drove a silver Chrysler 200 with stolen license plates to conceal the vehicle's identity. Surveillance data and license-plate readers tracked Byrd from his Boynton Beach residence to the crime scene and back home. A search warrant executed on Byrd's vehicle uncovered a Post-It note containing the Camino Gardens address, Motiwalla's name, personal address and fiancée's name, along with 9mm magazines and ammunition. Cell phone data analysis revealed Byrd had surveilled Motiwalla's workplace. Motiwalla had filed a whistleblower complaint against his former employer, Innovative Partners L.P., in 2025. Byrd is being held at Palm Beach County Jail.

cards.headline: Woman found dead in Fort Pierce abandoned house was likely beaten to death
cards.teaser: A woman found dead in a Fort Pierce home was likely beaten to death in an abandoned house, police say.
cards.body:
A woman found dead in a Fort Pierce home was likely beaten to death in an abandoned house, according to police.

Police are working to determine the circumstances surrounding the woman's death. The case is being treated as a homicide investigation.

cards.headline: Former Indian River County middle school athletic director sentenced to 10 years in federal prison
cards.body:
A former Indian River County middle school athletic director has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison. The sentence was handed down Monday for the former school official.

The athletic director worked at a middle school in Indian River County before the federal charges were filed. Federal prosecutors pursued the case that led to the conviction and sentencing.

The 10-year prison term was imposed by a federal court. The case involved a former administrator who held a position of authority within the Indian River County school system.

The sentencing marks the conclusion of federal criminal proceedings against the former middle school athletic director. The individual will serve the decade-long sentence in federal custody.

cards.headline: Brightline and Tri-Rail offer transit options for World Cup matches at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens
cards.teaser: Brightline is the official transit partner for the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Miami, with round-trip tickets ranging from $76 to $150. Tri-Rail offers a cheaper alternative with one-way tickets from $2.50 to $6.90.
cards.body:
Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens will host seven World Cup matches starting Monday, June 15, when Saudi Arabia takes on Uruguay at 6 p.m. The last Miami match, the third-place match, is scheduled for Saturday, July 18 at 5 p.m. Transit options like Brightline and Tri-Rail could save travelers significant money compared to driving, as parking passes for Hard Rock Stadium cost as much as $200.

Brightline is the official transit partner for the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Miami. Round-trip tickets range from $76 to $150. From the Brightline Aventura Station, the designated transit hub closest to the stadium, Miami-Dade County will offer free Game Day Express shuttle buses directly to the stadium gates. Shuttles are first-come, first-served, and riders must show a valid World Cup match ticket for that specific day to board. Tri-Rail offers a cheaper alternative with one-way tickets ranging from $2.50 to $6.90, depending on the starting station. Weekend round-trip travel is available for $5. Fans can also reach the stadium via Metrorail or Metrobus by taking Metrorail or Tri-Rail to the Miami-Dade Golden Glades Interchange and connecting via Metrobus Route 297. Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft can drop passengers at designated rideshare zones at the stadium, though surge pricing and longer wait times are expected.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove neighborhood named one of America's fastest-growing areas
cards.body:
RentCafe recently recognized Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code as one of the fastest-growing in the country, with Southern Grove leading the charge. The neighborhood has transformed dramatically over the past decade, growing from barely existing to a thriving community. Housing inventory in Southern Grove has surged by 177 percent, representing one of Florida's largest growth spurts. The neighborhood has attracted significant attention for its educated population and notably high homeownership rates.

The neighborhood's rapid expansion is directly tied to its emergence as a major employment center. Large employers including FedEx and Amazon have established operations there, with Amazon demonstrating particular confidence in the area by closing its existing facility this year to construct a substantially larger replacement. This corporate investment has created jobs and economic momentum that continues to drive residential development and population growth throughout Southern Grove.

Southern Grove's success is not accidental but the result of intentional planning. The neighborhood was deliberately designed as one of four communities created to give residents compelling reasons to relocate and establish long-term roots. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's strong showing of up-and-coming communities reflects specific economic advantages. "Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California," Both explained. She also noted that ongoing infrastructure investment has fueled construction activity across many of the state's growing suburban areas.

Southern Grove is not alone in gaining recognition. Ponte Vedra Beach earned the top position on RentCafe's America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods list, celebrated for its appeal to families, retirees, and young professionals seeking a balanced lifestyle. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area have similarly achieved top-50 rankings, gaining recognition for their excellent schools and strong housing demand. These successes demonstrate Florida's broader appeal as a destination for residential growth and underscore why the state continues to attract families and professionals seeking new opportunities.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach Cape Verde fan heads to Miami for tiny island nation's first World Cup
cards.body:
Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is heading to Miami this month to witness a historic moment for his home country. Cape Verde, a small archipelago of 10 islands located off the African coast, has qualified for the World Cup for the first time in its history. The island nation, which has a population of only half a million people, will compete under the team name Tubarão Azul, or Blue Sharks.

Dacruz grew up in Cape Verde before relocating to the United States. He still has many family members living on the islands and says the World Cup qualification has been the dominant topic of conversation throughout the nation. Cape Verde gained independence from Portugal in the 1970s and is known for its beautiful beaches. When Dacruz was growing up, he played FIFA video games and recalls searching for Cape Verde players in the game, finding only about two listed. Making the World Cup will provide Cape Verde's soccer federation with more than $10 million to invest in developing future generations of players. Dacruz expressed his amazement at the achievement, saying "I didn't think that would happen in my lifetime because we're so small."

Dacruz will attend Cape Verde's match against Uruguay in Miami, having received tickets as an anniversary gift from his girlfriend. He described the gift as a special surprise, recalling that she presented him with a box containing a handwritten note saying "I'm going to the World Cup." Although Cape Verde opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites, Dacruz remains optimistic about his team's chances. He stated confidently that "We're there you know. All we have to do is win a couple of games and we'll get far."

The timing of Cape Verde's World Cup appearance also connects the island nation to American weather discussions. During hurricane season, meteorologist Sami Squires explains that Cape Verde is frequently mentioned in weather coverage. Tropical systems regularly form near the islands before tracking westward across the Atlantic toward the United States. According to Squires, "We get these waves that form across the coast of Africa and eventually track across the Atlantic." Dacruz is currently waiting to receive his newest Cape Verde national jersey to wear to the game this month, adding another layer of excitement to this historic moment for both the nation and its diaspora community.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove neighborhood named one of America's fastest-growing areas
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has earned recognition from RentCafe as one of the fastest-growing zip codes in the country, largely due to the explosive growth of the Southern Grove neighborhood. The area has undergone a remarkable transformation in just ten years, evolving from near nonexistence into a thriving residential and commercial center. Housing inventory in the neighborhood has surged by 177 percent, representing one of the largest growth spurts recorded across Florida.

The neighborhood's rapid expansion has been fueled by its emergence as a significant jobs hub. Major employers including FedEx and Amazon have established operations in Southern Grove, with Amazon demonstrating particular commitment to the area by planning to close its current facility later this year in order to construct a much larger replacement. Beyond job creation, the neighborhood has attracted residents based on other positive attributes. Southern Grove residents are notably well-educated, and the area boasts strong homeownership rates that helped it earn high marks in RentCafe's evaluation.

The growth in Southern Grove was not spontaneous. The neighborhood was intentionally designed as one of four distinct neighborhoods created to appeal to potential residents and encourage them to establish roots in Port St. Lucie. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's substantial number of emerging communities reflects several competitive advantages. She noted that the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California make it attractive to new residents. Additionally, ongoing infrastructure investment throughout the state has supported increased construction activity in developing suburbs across Florida.

Port St. Lucie was not alone among Florida communities recognized in RentCafe's report. Ponte Vedra Beach topped the organization's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list, earning praise for offering a balanced work-play atmosphere that appeals to families, retirees, and young professionals. Both Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also made the top 50, gaining recognition for their excellent schools and robust housing demand. These results underscore Florida's status as a state experiencing significant residential growth and development across multiple regions.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club $30 million renovation reaches 50 percent completion, on track for late 2026 reopening
cards.teaser: The historic golf course closed in November 2025 for a major makeover designed to restore its Donald Ross and Dick Wilson character while adding modern upgrades.
cards.body:
Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation has reached 50 percent completion as of early June, with city officials confirming the project remains on track for a November 2026 reopening. The course has been closed since November 2025 for the makeover designed to restore its historic character while providing modern upgrades. The original course was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson, and the city is working to preserve those historic elements. The north 9 holes, called the Wilson 9, are already fully grassed and growing in, while the south 9 holes, the Ross 9, are currently being grassed.

Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, recently toured the progress and said it exceeded her expectations. "I've been an advocate for improvement for a long time, and in all honesty, it's looking better than anticipated," Dunayer said. She added she is "so excited about what's happened and the opportunity to come back and play a virtually new golf course, but yet have the old integrity." However, Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn contacted WPTV expressing concerns that crews are opening large planting holes for trees near her home that could block her view of the golf course and negatively impact her property's value. The city says the $30 million budget has not changed since work began.

cards.headline: Four men rescue 324-pound injured sea turtle in Jupiter Sound, turtle dies hours later from boat strike injuries
cards.teaser: Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony were boating in Jupiter Sound when they spotted the adult female green sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway with severe injuries.
cards.body:
Four friends enjoying a day on the water in Jupiter Sound became unlikely heroes when they spotted a 324-pound adult female green sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway. Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony worked together to tie a rope around the turtle's shell and guide her toward Blowing Rocks Marina. The rescue required significant effort from all four men to pull the injured animal from the water. Once out of the water, the turtle they named Zoey displayed severe injuries, with her shell covered in deep cuts and her head drooping weakly, clear signs of a boat strike. "You could tell she'd probably been fighting for hours out there," Anthony said.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded quickly to the marina and confirmed that Zoey had suffered severe injuries from a boat strike. Despite the team's heroic efforts and the marine center's care, Zoey died just hours later. According to NOAA, hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. every year, with many killed. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles. Adult sea turtles are particularly vulnerable during nesting season, which runs in Florida from March through October.

Diana Cowan Kempton, the club's program director, said she hopes chess will help develop the next generation by building leaders who are more focused, patient, strategic and thoughtful in their decision making.

The club is attracting players of all skill levels. More than 36 juniors have already joined at the Port St. Lucie location. Thomas Furlong, a father who brought his children to the club, said the setting is ideal for his family. The Atlantis Chess Club now meets there every Friday. For Francesca Furlong, one of the club's newest members, the best part is playing with other kids. The club will soon begin two more programs at the Fenn Center in Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office increases presence at Wellington Green Mall after teen takeover post
cards.teaser: A social media post promoting a teen takeover at the Wellington Green Mall gained nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to increase law enforcement presence.
cards.body:
A social media post promoting a teen takeover at Wellington Green Mall garnered nearly 100,000 views, prompting the Palm Beach County Sheriff's Office to increase its law enforcement presence at the mall. Shoppers noticed the heightened police presence on Friday. Savanna Restrepo, who was there picking up her son Isaac from summer camp, said she had seen posts circulating online about the event beforehand and found the visible police presence reassuring. Fellow parent Eric Delgado said the law enforcement response was the right call.

Palm Beach County Commissioner Greg Weiss said community safety is a priority but pointed to a root cause: with school out and teens having more time on their hands, parents should be taking steps to fill that time. Weiss noted that Palm Beach County offers scholarship opportunities for summer camps and mentioned that community recreation centers offer programming throughout the day. He emphasized the importance of parental involvement, saying parents should know what their kids are doing and stay in contact with them.

cards.headline: Pride on the Block raises funds for Transpire Help in West Palm Beach
cards.teaser: Pride on the Block filled The Peach in West Palm Beach on Saturday, serving as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a nonprofit providing services to LGBTQ+ individuals.
cards.body:
Pride on the Block, held Saturday at The Peach in West Palm Beach, served as the largest fundraiser for Transpire Help, a nonprofit providing substance use treatment, mental health care, and stable housing to LGBTQ+ individuals. Donna Weinberger, founder of Transpire Help, said the event creates a space where attendees can feel celebrated and experience unity, joy, and safety together.

For performer Liam Chambers, the event held deep personal meaning. Chambers, a drag king who is three years sober, credited Transpire Help with turning his life around. Weinberger emphasized that the organization's services are especially critical because a significant portion of the community, particularly gender diverse people, lack health insurance or funds to access treatment otherwise. The fundraiser has become increasingly important as cuts to government funding have slashed the number of people Transpire Help can assist in half. Jack Cesivon, an LGBTQ+ community member, said the organization has helped people who have nobody else.

cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code was named one of the fastest-growing in the country by RentCafe, driven by explosive growth in the Southern Grove neighborhood.
cards.body:
Southern Grove, a neighborhood in Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code that barely existed a decade ago, has emerged as one of the fastest-growing areas in the country according to RentCafe. The neighborhood has become a major jobs hub, attracting employers like FedEx and Amazon. Amazon is so committed to the area that it is closing its current facility later this year to build an even larger one. Housing inventory in Southern Grove has exploded by 177 percent, marking one of the largest growth spurts in all of Florida. The neighborhood earned high marks for its educated residents and strong homeownership rates.

Southern Grove was deliberately designed as one of four neighborhoods meant to give people compelling reasons to move to the area and stay. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California. Sustained infrastructure investment has also fueled construction activity in many of these growing suburbs. Port St. Lucie is not the only Florida community earning recognition. Ponte Vedra Beach claimed the number one spot on RentCafe's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list, while Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also cracked the top 50.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club $30 million renovation reaches halfway point
cards.teaser: The Delray Beach Golf Club renovation project is 50 percent complete as of early June and remains on track to finish by the end of 2026, city officials say.
cards.body:
The Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation has reached the halfway point as of early June, with the course remaining closed since November 2025. City officials say the project is on track to reopen by the end of 2026, with the north 9 holes, called the Wilson 9, already fully grassed and growing in. The south 9 holes, known as the Ross 9, are currently being grassed. The makeover is designed to restore the historic character of the original course, which was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson, while giving it a modern upgrade.

Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, said the renovation is looking better than anticipated after she got a sneak peek at the progress. "I think it's going to be a bit more difficult because of some of the changes they've made to the bunkers and stuff like that, but it looks absolutely magnificent," Dunayer said. However, not all residents support the changes. Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn contacted WPTV expressing concern that crews are opening large planting holes for trees near her home that could block her view of the golf course and negatively impact her property's value. The city says the $30 million budget has not changed since work began.

hero.headline: Beetlejuice musical runs through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit brings spooky humor and over-the-top visuals to the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall with performances through this weekend.
hero.body:
Beetlejuice the musical is playing at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach through June 7. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film. The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen, whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble.

Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. He gets to break the fourth wall and communicate directly to the audience. Very early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when his wig change went wrong. He was wearing two wigs and the second wig came off with the first wig, so he was bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50, and are available at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: Over 100 paddlers to cross 80 miles of ocean from Bahamas to Lake Worth Beach for cystic fibrosis
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean this June in the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. Event founder Travis Suit said participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Piper's Angels Foundation, which Suit established to honor his daughter Piper, diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4. Suit, an avid paddler, was inspired to create the event after learning about the natural respiratory benefits of ocean salt air.

The crossing is part of a four-day schedule beginning June 10, with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove on the opening day. Thursday features a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner. Friday brings a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before the launch. All paddlers must wear a U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation device, waterproof whistle, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and active at all times, with mandatory safety meetings held before departure. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000, while crew or virtual participants have a $500 minimum, due by July 31. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to cheer paddlers during a daylong celebration. More information is available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: Annette Taddeo launches campaign to unseat Florida CFO Blaise Ingoglia
hero.body:
Former Florida state Senator Annette Taddeo announced Monday she is running to unseat Republican Blaise Ingoglia as Chief Financial Officer, hoping to become the first Democrat elected to the position in two decades. Taddeo made her announcement at Second Baptist Church in Richmond Heights, the same location where she launched her successful 2017 Senate campaign that made her the first Latina Democrat elected to the Florida Senate. She released a campaign video alongside the announcement and spoke to a small group that included many members of the press.

At the church event, Taddeo criticized Ingoglia, whom Governor Ron DeSantis appointed CFO in July 2025, for failing to serve as a watchdog for Florida taxpayers. She pointed to the Everglades-based immigration detention center known as Alligator Alcatraz, which costs Florida taxpayers upwards of 1 billion dollars in service contracts, several awarded to DeSantis donors. She also highlighted insurance rates rising in Florida at roughly double the national rate and referenced the Hope Florida scandal, in which the DeSantis administration directed millions in Medicaid settlement dollars to the Governor's wife's nonprofit, which later rerouted the money to political committees aimed at defeating ballot measures supporting abortion and recreational adult-use cannabis. Taddeo characterized Ingoglia as a lapdog for the Governor rather than a watchdog for Floridians and criticized him for not auditing millions of dollars in no-bid contracts awarded to donors, which she said is required by Florida law.

Ingoglia has spent months touring the state highlighting what he describes as wasteful local government spending. His efforts have been used to justify recently passed legislation to slash homestead property taxes, which will require 60 percent approval on the November ballot and would increase homestead property tax exemptions for residents to 250,000 dollars by 2028. Taddeo framed this initiative as an attempt by Republican policymakers to convince voters that the party has addressed cost-of-living issues after controlling Florida's government for three decades.

Taddeo, born in Colombia, fled to the United States after terrorists kidnapped her father. She won a special election for Florida Senate in September 2017 and retained her seat in the 2018 general election. She ran unsuccessfully for Miami-Dade Clerk and Comptroller in 2024, losing to Republican incumbent Juan Fernandez-Barquin. However, Taddeo must first win a Democratic primary against Earle Ford, a U.S. Army veteran, before facing Ingoglia in the general election. A late-April poll commissioned by Ruth's List Florida found she would lead Ingoglia in a head-to-head matchup for CFO.

cards.headline: Apollo Beach lawmaker Michael Owen endorses Byron Donalds for Florida Governor
cards.teaser: State Representative Michael Owen became the newest Florida lawmaker to support Congressman Byron Donalds in the race for Governor, describing him as a leader who can make government more efficient for taxpayers.
cards.body:
Michael Owen, a Republican lawmaker from Apollo Beach who represents parts of Hillsborough and Manatee counties, endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor in a statement released Monday. Owen said Donalds will lead with a Florida First mindset and work to address challenges while making government leaner and more efficient for taxpayers. Owen joins a growing list of national and state Republicans supporting Donalds, including President Donald Trump, U.S. Senator Rick Scott, and many members of Congress and the Florida Legislature. Owen was first elected in 2024.

Donalds holds a commanding fundraising lead in the Republican Primary, with his campaign and the Friends of Byron Donalds political committee raising $81 million by May. Polls have consistently shown Donalds near 50 percent in the Republican Primary, while most other candidates remain in single digits. In a potential General Election matchup against likely Democratic nominee David Jolly, Donalds has a small lead in most polls, though a May Change Research survey of 1,593 likely voters showed Jolly ahead 46 percent to 42 percent, with a 2.3 percent margin of error. Few lawmakers have supported Donalds' opponents, including former House Speaker Paul Renner, endorsed by former Senate President Pro Tempore Dennis Baxley. Florida's Primary Election is scheduled for August 18.

cards.headline: Miami-Dade Commissioner Rene Garcia backs Jay Collins for Florida Governor
cards.teaser: Miami-Dade County Commissioner Rene Garcia announced his endorsement of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins during the kickoff rally for Collins' Freedom Tour at La Carreta in Hialeah.
cards.body:
Miami-Dade County Commissioner René Garcia announced his endorsement of Lt. Governor Jay Collins in the 2026 Florida Governor's race during Collins' Freedom Tour kickoff rally at La Carreta in Hialeah. Garcia, a former state Representative and Senator who represents Miami-Dade County Commission District 13, stated that "Florida doesn't need another politician. It needs a proven leader." He praised Collins' military service and record in public office, saying Collins "understands that government works for the people, not the other way around." Collins' campaign described Garcia as "one of the most prominent elected officials in South Florida to endorse Collins, further strengthening the campaign's growing support across the state."

Collins, a former Green Beret and current Lieutenant Governor, welcomed Garcia's backing, saying "René has spent decades fighting for the people of Miami-Dade County and understands what leadership looks like." Collins positioned himself as the candidate best equipped to continue conservative policies enacted under term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis. He noted that "Florida's success didn't happen by accident. We built the strongest economy in the nation, stood up for freedom when others backed down, and became the blueprint for conservative governance." Collins faces competition from Trump-endorsed U.S. Congressman Byron Donalds, who leads in fundraising and polling, along with former House Speaker Paul Renner and James Fishback for the GOP nomination.

cards.headline: Republican Bryan Leib withdraws from Congressional District 25 race, endorses Donalds for Governor
cards.teaser: Hollywood Republican Bryan Leib announced he will not run against Congressman Jared Moskowitz in Congressional District 25, instead dedicating his time to supporting Congressman Byron Donalds' gubernatorial campaign.
cards.body:
Republican Bryan Leib, a Hollywood media consultant and co-founder of Henry Public Relations, announced he will not run for Congress in Florida's 25th Congressional District this cycle. After prayer and conversations with friends, donors, community leaders, elected officials, and supporters across South Florida, Leib decided to sit out the race against Democratic U.S. Representative Jared Moskowitz of Parkland. Leib had previously challenged U.S. Representative Debbie Wasserman Schultz. Instead of running, Leib said he will dedicate his time to helping keep Florida the greatest state in America.

Leib announced his full endorsement of U.S. Byron Donalds for Governor, calling him a proven conservative leader and fighter. Donalds had notably endorsed Leib's congressional run in 2024. Running in the newly drawn Congressional District 25 would have meant entering a crowded GOP primary field that already includes former banking professional Dan Franzese, former state Representative George Moraitis, and former Boca Raton Mayor Scott Singer. Moskowitz said he will seek a third term in Congress, though the district where he won election twice was effectively dismantled under the new map. In the newly drawn CD 25, about 54 percent of voters supported Republican Donald Trump in 2024, compared to 52 percent who supported Democrat Joe Biden there in 2020.

cards.headline: Daisy Morales files for House District 43, setting up Democratic Primary with Samuel Vilchez Santiago
cards.teaser: Former state Representative Daisy Morales filed Monday to run for House District 43 in eastern Orange County, her third consecutive state race after losing re-election in 2022 and a rematch challenge in 2024.
cards.body:
After losing two consecutive state races, Daisy Morales is entering the race for House District 43, which covers eastern Orange County north of Lake Nona and south of Colonial Drive. Representative Johanna Lopez is vacating the seat to run for Orange County Board of Commissioners. Morales filed for the office Monday and will face Democrat Samuel Vilchez Santiago in the Democratic Primary, with the winner advancing to face Republican Robert Prater in November. In 2022, Morales lost her re-election bid in House District 44 to Rita Harris after the Democratic establishment withdrew support. Morales had angered party leadership by sometimes siding with Republicans, and others raised questions about her financial reports and residency. She also made headlines for attempting to get an Orlando Sentinel journalist fired over coverage she deemed biased. In 2024, Morales challenged Harris again as the challenger while Harris held the incumbent seat, losing with Harris receiving 65 percent of the vote.

Vilchez Santiago has secured endorsements from Lopez, Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings, and Orlando Mayor Buddy Dyer. Additional Central Florida Democrats backing his campaign include State Attorney Monique Worrell, Public Defender Melissa Vickers, Property Appraiser Amy Mercado, Comptroller Phil Diamond, and Tax Collector Scott Randolph. Vilchez Santiago announced Monday that he has raised more than $160,000, including approximately $32,000 in the second quarter. He is on a leave of absence from the Orange County Democrats to run for the state House.

cards.headline: Four Florida congressmen endorse Belinda Keiser in Congressional District 22 Republican Primary
cards.teaser: Republican Congressmen Aaron Bean, Neal Dunn, Randy Fine, and Jimmy Patronis announced their support for Belinda Keiser as qualifying week begins in the increasingly crowded Republican Primary for Congressional District 22.
cards.body:
Four Republican members of Florida's Congressional Delegation are endorsing Belinda Keiser, Vice Chancellor of Keiser University, in her race for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. U.S. Reps Aaron Bean, Neal Dunn, Randy Fine and Jimmy Patronis are backing Keiser as she competes in an increasingly crowded Republican Primary. Bean, who has known Keiser for years, praised her as an energetic worker who has given her time and talent to education in Florida. Dunn, who is leaving office after this term, said Keiser has served the state well through her private sector work, which has helped propel many young professionals into the workforce. Fine called Keiser a champion for Florida's higher education system and the future of every Florida student. Patronis, the newest member of Congress to support Keiser, called her a friend and a fighter who does everything with excellence.

Keiser is running to replace Debbie Wasserman Schultz, who opted to run in Florida's 20th Congressional District instead of the newly drawn CD 22. Under Keiser's leadership, Keiser University has become one of Florida's largest not-for-profit universities, educating more than 20,000 students across 18 Florida campuses and employing more than 4,000 team members. The newly reconfigured CD 22 stretches coast to coast, from Marco Island in Southwest Florida to the Atlantic coast. Keiser was a Florida Presidential Elector to the U.S. Electoral College in 2024, casting a ballot for President Donald Trump, and served as a Florida at-large delegate to the 2024 Republican National Convention.

cards.headline: Martin Hyde launches independent campaign for Florida Senate District 22
cards.teaser: Former congressional candidate Martin Hyde announced he will run as an independent to succeed term-limited state Senator Joe Gruters in Senate District 22, joining a field of five candidates.
cards.body:
Martin Hyde, a Sarasota activist, announced his independent campaign for Florida Senate District 22 in a Facebook video, acknowledging a viral video from four and a half years ago in which he chastised a female police officer during a traffic stop and threatened her commanding officer's career. Hyde previously made failed runs against U.S. Rep. Vern Buchanan in a 2022 Republican Primary and for Sarasota City Commission. He is now one of five candidates filed in the district, which will be vacated by term-limited state Sen. Joe Gruters. James Buchanan, son of the sitting congressman, and Vic Rohe are competing for the Republican nomination, while Democrats Arianna O'Donnell and Lew Wasserman are filed to run in their primary.

Hyde said he is running against development interests that have secured major legislative victories through bills including SB 180, Live Local, and SB 399, which preempt local control. He noted his opponent has close to $2 million in campaign funds and questioned how contributors expect to recoup that money. The district leans significantly Republican, with more than 58 percent of voters supporting Donald Trump over Kamala Harris in the last presidential election. Hyde loaned $194,000 to his 2022 congressional campaign. A former professional soccer player for Brighton and Southampton, Hyde later became CEO of Gulf Business Services, which was acquired in 2022 by DEX Imaging.

hero.headline: 125-acre brush fire contained in western Martin County
hero.body:
Firefighters fully contained a 125-acre brush fire in western Martin County on Monday. The fire burned through rural land in the western part of the county before crews brought it under control.

The blaze posed challenges for firefighters working in the remote western section of Martin County. Crews worked to prevent the fire from spreading to additional acreage in the area.

Martin County fire officials confirmed the fire was fully contained on Monday afternoon. The containment means the fire perimeter has been secured and the blaze is no longer spreading.

The cause of the brush fire remains under investigation. Western Martin County contains large tracts of undeveloped land where brush fires can spread rapidly during dry conditions.

cards.headline: 36,000-square-foot mural now faces Florida Turnpike drivers in Martin County
cards.teaser: A massive mural spanning 36,000 square feet is now visible to drivers traveling on the Florida Turnpike through Martin County.
cards.body:
The large-scale artwork faces motorists using the turnpike as they pass through Martin County. The mural measures 36,000 square feet, making it one of the largest public art installations visible from the highway.

The installation adds a visual landmark for the thousands of drivers who travel the Florida Turnpike through Martin County daily. The turnpike is a major north-south route connecting South Florida to Central Florida.

Details about the artist, subject matter and exact location along the turnpike corridor were not provided. The mural represents a significant addition to public art visible to travelers in Martin County.

cards.headline: GOP gubernatorial candidates appear at Martin County Republican fundraiser
cards.teaser: Republican candidates for governor addressed supporters at a Martin County Republican Party fundraising event on Monday.
cards.body:
Multiple GOP gubernatorial hopefuls spoke at the Martin County Republican fundraiser as part of their campaigns for the 2026 governor's race. The event gave Republican voters in Martin County an opportunity to hear directly from candidates seeking their party's nomination.

The fundraiser took place on Monday as candidates continue campaigning ahead of the primary election. Martin County has traditionally been a Republican stronghold in Treasure Coast politics.

The appearance represents part of the candidates' efforts to build support and raise funds in counties across Florida. Additional details about which specific candidates attended and what they discussed at the Martin County event were not provided.

cards.headline: Delayed I-95 roadwork causes rush hour backups in Martin County
cards.teaser: Roadwork on Interstate 95 that ran behind schedule created significant traffic delays during Monday evening rush hour in Martin County.
cards.body:
Construction crews working on I-95 in Martin County failed to complete their work on schedule, resulting in major backups during the evening commute. The delayed roadwork affected drivers traveling through Martin County during peak traffic hours.

The timing of the construction delays coincided with rush hour, compounding traffic problems on the busy interstate corridor. I-95 serves as the primary north-south route through Martin County, carrying commuters and commercial traffic. The construction project represents one of several ongoing infrastructure improvements on I-95 through the Treasure Coast.

cards.headline: Florida Power & Light brings infrastructure upgrades to Martin County
cards.teaser: Florida Power & Light is implementing 2026 infrastructure improvements in Martin County as part of regional upgrades also covering St. Lucie and Indian River counties.
cards.body:
FPL is conducting infrastructure upgrades across Martin County in 2026 as part of a broader improvement program spanning the Treasure Coast. The utility company is making improvements to its electrical infrastructure in Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties.

The infrastructure work is designed to enhance the reliability and capacity of the electrical grid serving Martin County residents and businesses. FPL serves as the primary electricity provider for most of Martin County.

Specific details about the scope, cost and timeline of the Martin County upgrades were not provided. Infrastructure improvements typically include upgrades to power lines, substations and other equipment that delivers electricity to customers.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast High plays Martin County High in football August 21
cards.teaser: Treasure Coast High School is scheduled to face Martin County High School in a football matchup set for August 21.
cards.body:
The two Treasure Coast high schools will meet on the gridiron on August 21 in what promises to be a key early-season game. Treasure Coast High School and Martin County High School represent two of the region's football programs.

The game will take place as teams begin their 2026 football seasons. Both schools compete in Florida high school football and draw support from their respective communities on the Treasure Coast.

Additional details about game time, location and whether this is a regular season or preseason contest were not provided. High school football games draw significant community interest across Martin and St. Lucie counties.

cards.headline: Teenager on e-scooter collides with patrol vehicle in Florida after running stop sign
cards.teaser: Dashcam footage captured the moment a teenager riding an e-scooter crashed into a police patrol vehicle after driving through a stop sign, according to Florida police.
cards.body:
Police dashcam video shows a teenager on an electric scooter colliding with a patrol vehicle at an intersection. The teen failed to stop at a stop sign before the collision occurred, according to law enforcement.

The dashcam footage documents the moment of impact between the e-scooter and the patrol vehicle. Police released the video showing the traffic violation and subsequent crash.

Details about injuries, the specific Florida agency involved, the exact location of the incident and any charges filed were not provided. The incident highlights ongoing concerns about e-scooter safety and compliance with traffic laws.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove neighborhood named one of America's fastest-growing areas
hero.body:
Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has been named one of the fastest-growing zip codes in the country by RentCafe, driven by the Southern Grove neighborhood that barely existed a decade ago. The area has experienced remarkable housing growth, with inventory expanding by 177 percent, representing one of the largest growth spurts across Florida. The neighborhood has earned recognition for its educated residents and strong homeownership rates, making it an attractive destination for those seeking to relocate.

The expansion of Southern Grove has transformed it into a major employment center. Large employers including FedEx and Amazon have established operations in the area, with Amazon demonstrating particular confidence in the neighborhood's future. The company is closing its current facility this year to construct a substantially larger facility in Southern Grove, signaling long-term commitment to the region's development.

The growth of Southern Grove was not organic but rather the result of deliberate planning. The neighborhood was designed as one of four communities specifically created to offer compelling reasons for people to move to the area and establish roots there. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, "Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California." Both noted that sustained infrastructure investment has also contributed significantly to construction activity across many of these developing suburbs.

Port St. Lucie is not alone in experiencing this growth surge within Florida. Ponte Vedra Beach earned the number one position on RentCafe's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list, noted for offering an ideal balance between work and leisure that attracts families, retirees, and young professionals. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also achieved recognition within the top 50 neighborhoods, with both communities highlighted for their excellent schools and strong housing demand. This concentration of rapidly developing communities reflects broader trends reshaping Florida's landscape as more people and businesses choose to relocate to the state.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie man arrested for swinging bat at children riding bicycles
cards.teaser: A Port St. Lucie man was arrested after police say he swung a bat at children riding bicycles.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie man faces charges after allegedly swinging a bat at children riding bicycles. The arrest occurred Monday.

Police arrested the man following the incident involving the children. The case remains under investigation.

cards.headline: Woman found dead in Fort Pierce abandoned house was likely beaten to death
cards.teaser: A woman found dead in a Fort Pierce home was likely beaten to death in an abandoned house, police say.
cards.body:
A woman found dead in a Fort Pierce home was likely beaten to death in an abandoned house, according to police.

Police are working to determine the circumstances surrounding the woman's death. The case is being treated as a homicide investigation.

cards.headline: Downtown Fort Pierce visitors face hefty citations for parking more than 2 hours
cards.teaser: Downtown Fort Pierce guests are receiving hefty parking citations for staying longer than two hours.
cards.body:
Visitors to downtown Fort Pierce are facing significant fines for parking longer than two hours. The citations are being issued as part of parking enforcement in the downtown area.

The enforcement affects guests visiting downtown Fort Pierce businesses and attractions. The two-hour limit is now being actively monitored and enforced.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office swears in junior deputies
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office held a swearing-in ceremony for junior deputies.
cards.body: The junior deputy program allows young residents to participate in law enforcement activities. The newly sworn-in junior deputies will serve in the program under the guidance of the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

cards.headline: Florida Power & Light brings 2026 infrastructure upgrades to St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Florida Power & Light is implementing infrastructure upgrades in St. Lucie County as part of 2026 improvements.
cards.body:
Florida Power & Light is bringing infrastructure upgrades to Indian River, St. Lucie and Martin Counties in 2026. The improvements are part of the utility's ongoing infrastructure enhancement program.

The upgrades will affect customers across the three-county area. Florida Power & Light is implementing the improvements to enhance service reliability and capacity.

cards.headline: Blaring sounds in St. Lucie County explained
cards.teaser: Residents hearing loud sounds in St. Lucie County now have an explanation for the noise.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County residents have been hearing blaring sounds in the area. Officials have identified the source of the noise.

The sounds have prompted questions from residents across St. Lucie County. Authorities have provided an explanation for what is causing the loud noises.

hero.headline: Former Indian River County middle school athletic director sentenced to 10 years in federal prison
hero.body:
A former Indian River County middle school athletic director has been sentenced to 10 years in federal prison. The sentence was handed down Monday for the former school official.

The athletic director worked at a middle school in Indian River County before the federal charges were filed. Federal prosecutors pursued the case that led to the conviction and sentencing.

The 10-year prison term was imposed by a federal court. The case involved a former administrator who held a position of authority within the Indian River County school system.

The sentencing marks the conclusion of federal criminal proceedings against the former middle school athletic director. The individual will serve the decade-long sentence in federal custody.

cards.headline: Gas prices change in Sebastian over past week
cards.teaser: Gas prices in Sebastian have fluctuated during the past seven days.
cards.body:
Sebastian gas prices shifted over the course of the last week. The price changes occurred between June 1 and June 8.

Drivers in Sebastian experienced variations at the pump during the one-week period. The changes reflect movement in local fuel costs for the coastal Indian River County community.

cards.headline: Mary Lou Brown of Vero Beach dies
cards.teaser: Mary Lou Brown, a Vero Beach resident, has died.
cards.body: The Vero Beach resident's death was announced Monday. Brown was a member of the Indian River County community.

cards.headline: Four men rescue injured 324-pound sea turtle near Jupiter
cards.teaser: Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony pulled a boat-struck green sea turtle from Jupiter Sound, but the animal later died.
cards.body:
Four friends boating in Jupiter Sound spotted a 324-pound adult female green sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway and sprang into action. Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony carefully tied a rope around the turtle's shell and guided her toward Blowing Rocks Marina. After pulling the turtle from the water, they named her Zoey and discovered the severity of her injuries. Her shell was covered in deep cuts and her head drooped weakly, indicating she had been struck by a boat. "You could tell she'd probably been fighting for hours out there," Anthony said.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded to the marina and confirmed Zoey had suffered severe injuries from a boat strike. Despite the team's rescue efforts and the marine center's care, Zoey died just hours later. According to NOAA, hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. every year. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles. Adult sea turtles are particularly vulnerable to vessel strikes during nesting season, which runs from March through October in Florida.

cards.headline: Stuart business owner says permit for storage building has taken nearly two years, cost $40,000
cards.teaser: Janet Milici, co-owner of Natural Flow Impact Windows and Doors in Stuart, says obtaining a permit for a 30-by-40-foot storage building has become an expensive, lengthy ordeal.
cards.body:
Janet Milici, co-owner of Natural Flow Impact Windows and Doors, says a permit for a storage building behind her Stuart business has become a nearly two-year ordeal costing her roughly $40,000. Milici first applied in 2024 for the 30-by-40-foot structure, intended to provide secure storage for business materials and not part of an expansion project. The permitting process required her to complete engineering studies, environmental reviews, traffic analyses and pay for turtle relocation. "People try to cut corners and do things without permitting, but we are trying to do everything right," Milici said. She shared her frustrations after attending a recent Let's Hear It community meet-up in Jensen Beach.

While the permit has recently been approved, Milici says additional city fees continue as the project moves through final stages. She expressed concern that delays during hurricane season are leaving materials exposed outdoors and putting her business at risk. "If I can't put my materials in a safe place, then it's going to cost me, it's going to put me out of business if you really want to know," Milici said. WPTV reached out to the City of Stuart Planning and Zoning department about the permitting process for storage buildings within city limits and is awaiting a response.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie Southern Grove neighborhood ranks among fastest-growing areas in America
cards.teaser: RentCafe named Port St. Lucie zip code 34987 one of the fastest-growing in the country, driven by the Southern Grove neighborhood.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has been named one of the fastest-growing in the entire country by RentCafe, driven largely by Southern Grove, a neighborhood that barely existed ten years ago. Southern Grove has become a major jobs hub, attracting big-name employers like FedEx and Amazon. Amazon is closing its current facility later this year to build an even larger one in the area. Housing inventory in Southern Grove has exploded by 177 percent, one of the largest growth spurts in all of Florida. The neighborhood earned high marks for its educated residents and strong homeownership rates.

Southern Grove was deliberately designed as one of four neighborhoods created to give people compelling reasons to move to Port St. Lucie and stay. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California. Sustained infrastructure investment has also fueled construction activity in many of these growing suburbs.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach man to cheer Cape Verde at World Cup in Miami
cards.teaser: Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach will attend Cape Verde's World Cup match against Uruguay in Miami, celebrating his home country's first-ever World Cup appearance.
cards.body:
Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is headed to Miami this month to cheer on Cape Verde at the World Cup. Dacruz grew up in Cape Verde, an archipelago of 10 islands off the African coast, before moving to the U.S. The island nation, which he describes as having amazing beaches, has a population of only half a million people and is making its first-ever World Cup appearance. Cape Verde's team is known as the Tubarão Azul, or Blue Sharks. Dacruz, who has many family members still living in Cape Verde, says the team's qualification has been the talk of the island.

Dacruz will attend Cape Verde's game against Uruguay in Miami in person, a gift from his girlfriend on their anniversary. She gave him a handwritten note during their anniversary dinner that said he was going to the World Cup. Cape Verde opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites. Making the World Cup will provide the nation's soccer federation with more than $10 million to help develop the next generation of players. During hurricane season, the islands are frequently referenced in weather coverage as tropical systems often form near Cape Verde before tracking west across the Atlantic toward the U.S.
